input.question: Why do we instinctively rub an area that gets hurt?
input.ground_truth: From the standpoint of the nervous system: distraction. Rubbing the area around an injury stimulates sensory neurons and creates a sort of "background noise." You'll still feel the pain from the injury, but it's sort of muffled.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a boo-boo on your knee after you bump it.

When you hurt a part of your body, your body sends a message to your brain that says, "Ouch, something's wrong here!" To help make that ouch feeling better, your brain tells your hand to rub that spot.

Rubbing helps because it can:

1. Make the blood flow a little more to that spot, which brings in some healing helpers.
2. Distract your brain a little from the ouch feeling.
3. Sometimes, it just feels better because it's gentle and warm.

So, when you rub a hurt spot, your body is trying to help you feel better!
